title: Tools, resources, prompts
intro: A server can offer more than tools. The triple — and who reaches for each — is MCP's most confusable idea.

steps.title: The triple
steps.body: The client **invokes tools**, **queries resources**, and **interpolates prompts**; the server exposes all three.

points.label: Tools
points.note: Functions the client can invoke — retrieve/search, send a message, update DB records. Actions, possibly with side effects; the model decides to use them.

points.label: Resources
points.note: READ-ONLY data exposed by the server — files, database records, API responses. Like GET endpoints: data out, no significant computation, no side effects.

points.label: Prompts
points.note: Pre-defined, well-tested templates for AI interactions — document Q&A, transcript summary, output-as-JSON. User-triggered.

steps.title: Resources: URIs, direct and templated
steps.body:
```python
@mcp.resource("papers://folders")          # direct/static URI
def get_available_folders() -> str: ...

@mcp.resource("papers://{topic}")          # templated URI, filled at runtime
def get_topic_papers(topic: str) -> str: ...
```

The URI uniquely identifies the resource; set **mime_type** to hint what's coming back (strings, JSON, binary…).

steps.title: Prompts: ship your best one
steps.body:
A prompt is a set of User/Assistant messages the client interpolates — **high quality and well-tested**, authored once on the server instead of improvised by every user.

In the course chatbot: `/prompts` lists them, `/prompt <name> <args>` executes one; resources surface as **@-mentions** (`@folders`, `@ai_interpretability`). Tools need no UI at all — the model reaches for them itself.

steps.title: The decision rule
steps.body:
> [!key] **Side effects or model initiative → tool. Read-only context the app pulls in → resource. A reusable, tested recipe → prompt.**

The course's own example: fetching new papers from arXiv (writes files, model-initiated) is a *tool*; reading the already-saved `papers_info.json` is a *resource*; "generate a great search prompt for topic X" is a *prompt*.

recap:
**Invoke tools, query resources, interpolate prompts.**

- Tools: actions, side effects, model-initiated.
- Resources: GET-like read-only data; direct or templated URIs + mime types.
- Prompts: server-authored, user-triggered templates.
- UI tells: automatic (tools), @-mentions (resources), slash commands (prompts).
